info.description: Versioned contract for the HLD learning application. Simulation results are illustrative modeled runs.

413.description: request_too_large: raw API POST body exceeds the configured byte limit (default 256 KiB), including unknown-length/chunked bodies. No model executes.

422.description: result_too_large: complete serialized result exceeds the response limit. A structured error replaces the result; no partial successful JSON is sent. Reduce workload before retrying.

503.description: simulation_busy: all process-local run slots are occupied. Try again explicitly after the Retry-After hint; it does not guarantee capacity is free.

Retry-After.description: Retry hint in seconds. Capacity may remain occupied.

post.description: Simulation delivery uses process-local admission before body parsing (default two active requests across models), a bounded raw body, and bounded serialization of the entire result (default 4 MiB). These HTTP safeguards are outside modeled behavior. No queued or automatic retry is added; an admitted run keeps its existing model/schema semantics.

get.description: Draft workshops are accessible by direct link, excluded from ordinary published discovery. This endpoint serves educational content; it creates no short links.

404.description: No authored case study with this ID

get.description: Published, startup-validated case-study metadata in catalog order, then ID. Draft and planned entries are omitted. Returns an empty array when none are published. Explicit draft detail routes remain available.

get.summary: Search published concepts and workshop stages
get.description: Packaged public content only. Literal terms must all occur in title, summary or plain body text. Title matches precede summary then body; ties use catalog order and stable IDs, preserving workshop stage order. Draft/planned content and learner answers are excluded. Unknown/repeated filters return 400. Returns at most 20 results with the total match count.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Blank returns no results; otherwise 2–100 UTF-16 code units. Searches all whitespace-separated terms as literal substrings, ignoring case and compatibility character forms.

post.description: Strict closed retry input with exact integral JSON tokens, duplicate-key and trailing-root rejection. checkpointsPath.description: Present only with the guided capability.

workshopPath.description: Present for authored case-study entries; absent for topics.

checkpoints.description: Guided simulation checkpoints; empty unless the topic has the guided capability.

target.description: Select exactly one identity family: cache operation, capacity job ID, delivery messageId/attemptId, data-access operationId, or transaction stepId (reservation or atomicity). Retry requestId selects request-level evidence or pairs with its actual attemptId. Kind and occurrence select actual Java evidence; each untimed operation/step has one outcome.

oneOf.description: Delivery target requires a semantic message/attempt pair. Attempt identity must equal messageId followed by -a1 through -a5; content and Java validators enforce this association. Its closed kind vocabulary is checked against actual delivery event selector capabilities during generation.
Select the one actual data-access outcome for a unique operation ID and its kind. This is untimed outcome evidence, not a fabricated simulation event; unique operation IDs require occurrence 1.

Select the one actual reservation or atomicity outcome for a unique scheduled step ID and its returned kind. Content validation checks the selected model's own closed kind vocabulary and required step identity. Outcomes are untimed; unique step IDs require occurrence 1, without a fabricated event or authored array position.

Select actual retry request-level evidence without an attempt identity. Kind and occurrence select returned Java events; content and Java validators enforce the model-specific capability and identity association.

Select actual retry attempt evidence using its original request and matching -a1 through -a5 identity. Kind and occurrence select returned Java events; content and Java validators enforce the model-specific capability and identity association.

GuidedCheckpoint.description: One predict -> reveal -> explain -> choose step. Its target selects actual Java evidence by exactly one identity family, kind and occurrence; never by narration or authored array index.

failureSchedule.description: Optional failure schedule for model version 1.1.1. Not allowed with model version 1.0.0.

timestamp.description: Server error time; external metadata, excluded from simulation replay.

entityId.description: Stable identifier of the entity that fails (e.g. Node A)

failAtMs.description: Virtual time in milliseconds when the failure occurs

recoverAtMs.description: Virtual time when the entity recovers; null means permanent failure for this run

inFlightBehavior.description: What happens to work already assigned at failure time

hitOrMiss.description: ERROR means origin unavailable. A MISS or BYPASS with null returnedValue means key not found; absent keys are not cached.

hitRatio.description: Hits divided by hits + misses observed in the trace; bypass excluded, failed misses included. Zero when no eligible lookup exists.

version.description: Origin version the entry was filled from.

expiresAtMs.description: A lookup at or after this time misses.

CacheAsideInitialState.description: State before the first event. The cache starts empty; availability is constant for the run.

requestId.description: The operation the event belongs to, as "Operation N" in input order.

operation.description: 1-based position of the operation in the submitted input.

key.description: The cache key the event applies to.

cacheEntry.description: The key's cache entry after this event; absent when the cache holds no entry.

originValue.description: The key's committed origin value after this event; absent when the origin has no such key.

CacheAsideEvent.description: A trace event with the state of its key immediately after the event. Applying each event's key state over initialState reconstructs the full cache and origin state; never parse message.

CacheAsideLimits.description: Exact input bounds the Java model enforces. Clients validate against these instead of repeating them.

maxLatencyMs.description: Largest cache lookup or origin read latency, in milliseconds.

maxOperations.description: Largest number of operations in one run.

maxOperationTimeMs.description: Latest operation arrival time, in milliseconds.

maxValueLength.description: Longest initial or updated value, in characters.

QueueCapacityInput.title: Queue capacity simulation input
QueueCapacityInput.description: Input for the illustrative queues-tail-latency model. Java additionally validates nondecreasing arrivals and unique job IDs. Topic publication is independent of model registration. The HTTP API requires integral JSON tokens and rejects duplicate keys and trailing JSON values; JSON Schema validates the parsed value rather than token spelling.

QueueCapacityResult.title: Queue capacity simulation result
QueueCapacityResult.description: Authoritative typed post-event state for the illustrative worker-queue model. Nullable unavailable values may be omitted by the application mapper. Publication status belongs to the topic catalog.

DeliveryInput.title: Queue delivery domain input
DeliveryInput.description: Canonical input for the illustrative queues-delivery model, schema 1.0/model 1.0.0. Its OpenAPI component derives from this schema; topic publication belongs to the catalog. Arrays retain authored input order. Java additionally validates unique message/consumer IDs, referenced fault identities, unique loss selectors, alternating chronological failure schedules and ACK-before delay strictly less than processing time. JSON Schema validates parsed JSON values, not token spellings or duplicate JSON keys. The delivery HTTP controller separately rejects duplicate keys, trailing roots and nonintegral or coerced JSON tokens.

DeliveryResult.title: Queue delivery domain result
DeliveryResult.description: Canonical authoritative result for the illustrative queues-delivery model. Events contain typed post-event entity changes and optional committed ledger appends. Nullable unavailable fields may be omitted by the configured Java mapper. Independent lease/effect/ACK states do not imply exactly-once effects or vendor-specific broker behavior. Java checks causal identity equality, ordering, entity reconstruction, counter reconciliation and whole-batch prefix admission; JSON Schema checks shape and declared local conditions. OpenAPI and the lazy delivery client derive their shape validation from this canonical schema; catalog publication remains independent. Result observed/scheduled times use the conservative finite-input ceiling 60,000 + 100 deliveries × (60,000 lease + 1,000 processing + 1,000 ACK) = 6,260,000 ms; custom budgets may exceed the default 60,000 ms guard.

DataAccessInput.title: Data access analysis input
DataAccessInput.description: Canonical finite sequential access-path model. createdOrder is an ordering key, not time. Java additionally checks unique row/operation identities, enabled tenant-scoped business-key uniqueness and inclusive range order. JSON Schema validates parsed values; HTTP additionally rejects duplicate keys, trailing roots and coerced/nonintegral token spellings.

DataAccessResult.title: Data access analysis result
DataAccessResult.description: Complete authoritative finite analysis, without modeled latency or production benchmark claims. input references its canonical schema. Java owns evolving table state, access-path candidates, filtering before result limit, conflict precedence and work totals. JSON Schema enforces closed shape and local outcome discriminants; Java tests and frontend compatibility checks separately enforce semantic identities and captured-request correlation.

ReservationInput.title: Reservation interleaving model input
ReservationInput.description: Canonical complete caller-supplied interleaving for two illustrative reservation algorithms, schema 1.0/model 1.0.0. No time, randomness or database is modeled. Java additionally validates unique reservation/step identities, known references, schedule length twice actor count and exactly one READ followed by one ATTEMPT_RESERVE per actor before execution. JSON Schema validates parsed values; it cannot establish those identity/order relations or detect duplicate JSON keys and token spellings.

ReservationResult.title: Reservation interleaving model result
ReservationResult.description: Complete authoritative untimed reservation analysis. Captured input and all identities reference the canonical input owner. Closed outcome kinds distinguish reads, accepted reservations and business rejections; post-state retains prior observations. Completed describes schedule consumption, not invariant preservation or database commit. Unsafe allocated/accounted bounds intentionally permit values above initial units. Java tests own identity correlation, snapshot equality, arithmetic and first violating prefix semantics; JSON Schema establishes structure and local required/forbidden fields.

AtomicityInput.title: Transaction atomicity model input
AtomicityInput.description: Canonical finite complete interleaving for illustrative split writes and staged revision-checked publication. Java validates unique transaction/step IDs, references and the four legal complete per-actor programs before execution. Aborting or encountering insufficient stock in a legal program is a modeled result, not malformed input. JSON Schema validates parsed shape and bounds, not protocol order, duplicate JSON keys or integer token spelling. No clock, database or random choices are modeled.

AtomicityResult.title: Transaction atomicity model result
AtomicityResult.description: Complete authoritative untimed atomicity analysis. Public remaining and allocated units are guarded and together cannot exceed initial units; split writes may lose units and leak aborted effects but cannot create them. State bounds are 0..20, including unsafe partial states. Captured input and all IDs refer to the canonical input owner. Java owns mode-dependent private workspace presence, identity relationships, revision arithmetic, final/snapshot equality and invariant calculations. JSON Schema enforces closed local phase/outcome evidence and retained/cleared fields; it does not emulate transactions or promise durability.

RetryInput.title: Timeouts and retries model input
RetryInput.description: Canonical finite input for an illustrative caller retry policy and shared dependency worker queue. Java additionally validates unique original IDs, chronological arrival order and maxDelayMs >= baseDelayMs before any transition. Parsed JSON shape is not transport token spelling, duplicate-key or trailing-root validation. One run-local recorded random stream selects bounded FULL jitter delays; no network, cancellation, business effect, database or durability is modeled.

RetryResult.title: Timeouts and retries model result
RetryResult.description: Complete finite Java simulation evidence for caller wait state and independent dependency work. Captured input owns original IDs and controls. Initial and complete final state, closed event field categories and local caller/work phases are constrained here. Java owns identity/reference correspondence, scheduler ordering, arithmetic, exact event-prefix/final-state equality, policy behavior, metrics and replay. Same-callback causal microsteps may show completed work whose caller is still WAITING, before the following explicit request success; no other callback interleaves. No artificial partial result, business effect, idempotency, actual networking or durability is modeled.
